narrative:
The model predicts a 94% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that strongly align with employees who end up departing.

The three factors that influenced this decision most were your overall years of experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and the fact that you have received other job offers while working here. 

Your total professional experience of 6-10 years was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, half have only 1-5 years of experience, so your mid-level tenure signals higher mobility. Similarly, having spent 1-5 years in your current organization also pulled the prediction toward departure; this is actually the most common range even among stayers, but combined with your broader experience it suggests you are at a natural transition point.

The presence of external job opportunities was the third most influential factor and further increased the likelihood of leaving. While most employees the model predicts will stay have not received outside offers, you have, which the system interprets as a clear sign you may soon depart.

The organization should consider discussing retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths, better recognition of your contributions, or addressing the work-life balance and stress factors visible in your profile. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still meets your long-term goals.
